title: Runtime metadata anchoring and telemetry escrow playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the runtime metadata anchoring pattern and the telemetry escrow mechanism used across Redwood services to ensure reliable, auditable, and privacy-conscious observability. It complements our Telemetry Ingestion and Retention Guidelines by focusing on (1) how runtime-produced metadata is anchored to telemetry objects, (2) the escrow lifecycle for telemetry when downstream consumers are temporarily unavailable, and (3) operational procedures for recovery and audit.

Intended audience
- SREs and platform engineers operating the telemetry pipeline
- Service owners who emit metrics/traces/logs
- Security and compliance reviewers verifying retention/escrow controls

Motivation
- Observability gaps appear when runtime metadata (request ids, tenant context, model-version tags) is not reliably attached to telemetry or is lost during surges, leading to poor root cause analysis and billing mismatches.
- Backpressure and downstream outages in ingestion systems can result in data loss; a composable escrow model reduces permanent loss and preserves privacy constraints.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood production services that emit metrics, traces, structured logs, and prompt/response evaluation telemetry (hosted API, dedicated nodes, private deployments).
- Focuses on the telemetry pipeline components: telemetry-proxy, metric-forwarder, obs-ingester, telemetry-escrow-service, and slo-eval.
- Does NOT replace long-term archival/retention policies — it is an intermediate, bounded-duration buffer and metadata governance layer.

Definitions
- Anchored telemetry: telemetry record that includes a signed metadata envelope linking the record to runtime context (request_id, model_variant, tenant_id, sampling_bucket, ingestion_fingerprint).
- Telemetry escrow: temporary, encrypted storage for anchored telemetry records that cannot be immediately accepted by downstream consumers. Escrow is time-bounded and audit-trailed.

Design principles
1) Metadata as first-class observable: every telemetry emission must include a metadata envelope (see schema example) produced at the edge (gateway or service-side telemetry-proxy) and carried with the record through the pipeline.
2) Deterministic fingerprinting: an HMAC fingerprint computed over the envelope + payload ensures integrity and de-dup checks.
3) Escrow boundedness and governance: escrow retention <= 7 days by default and subject to tenant/region policy. Telemetry in escrow must be encrypted with tenant-scoped keys when required.
4) Privacy-by-default: PII must be redacted before escrow; escrow stores only hashed/annotated prompt fingerprints when capture is necessary for debugging.
5) Observable escrow metrics and SLOs: escrow must expose ingestion-lag, escrow-fill, successful-forward-rate, and escrow-purge-rate.

Metadata envelope (YAML example)
---
version: 1
request_id: "r-8f3c2a"
tenant_id: "t-acme-corp"
model_variant: "redwood-v1-8bit-fp16"
emit_ts: "2025-09-12T14:12:23Z"
sampling_bucket: "sm-0.1"
ingestion_fingerprint: "hmac-sha256:abcd1234..."
pii_redaction: "true"
origin: "edge-proxy-us-west-2"
---

Fingerprinting example (pseudo-Bash)
```
PAYLOAD='{"metric":"token_latency_ms","value":42}'
ENVELOPE='version=1;request_id=r-8f3c2a;tenant_id=t-acme-corp;emit_ts=2025-09-12T14:12:23Z'
HMAC_KEY_ENV=TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY
HMAC=$(echo -n "$ENVELOPE|$PAYLOAD" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY" -binary | base64)
echo "hmac-sha256:$HMAC"
```

Operational contracts and SLOs
- Ingestion availability: obs-ingester external endpoint must be available 99.95% monthly.
- Escrow forward latency (p95): <= 30s under normal load; during backpressure p95 <= 2m.
- Telemetry completeness: anchored telemetry completeness for critical request flows >= 99.9% (5m window).
- Escrow retention TTL default: 7 days. For regulated tenants, TTL can be reduced to 24h or extended to 14 days with security review.

Configuration table (example defaults)
| component | default_queue_size | escrow_ttl | encryption | forward_retry_policy | alert_threshold |
| telemetry-proxy | 10k | n/a | edge -> platform TLS | immediate x3, exp-backoff 2m | queue_fill > 75% |
| metric-forwarder | 50k | n/a | TLS | immediate x5, dead-letter -> escrow | forward_fail_rate > 1% |
| obs-ingester | 200k | 0.5d | server-side TLS | accept or respond 503 | ingest_lag_p95 > 30s |
| telemetry-escrow-service | 500k | 7d | tenant-KMS | background-forward every 30s, quick-retry on healthy | escrow_fill > 50% of quota |

Escrow lifecycle (numbered procedure)
1) Emit: service calls telemetry-proxy to emit anchored telemetry envelope + payload.
2) Forward: telemetry-proxy attempts to forward to obs-ingester.
3) Retry: on transient 5xx/503/timeout, metric-forwarder retries per policy.
4) Escrow: if all retries exhausted or obs-ingester responds with capacity-denied status (code 429/509), metric-forwarder writes a minimal escrow record to telemetry-escrow-service. The escrow write must include envelope, encrypted payload pointer, and escrow-metadata.
5) Restore: escrow forwarder monitors obs-ingester health and replays escrowed items when capacity is available; replay must preserve original emit_ts and fingerprint.
6) Purge: after escrow_ttl, records are purged and a purge audit event emitted. Purge must be irreversible and logged for compliance.

Escrow record minimal schema (single-line JSON for wire)
{"envelope":"<base64-yaml>","payload_ref":"s3://escrow/tenant/t-acme/2025-09-12/xyz.gz","fingerprint":"hmac-sha256:abcd...","encrypted":true,"kms_key_id":"arn:aws:kms:..."}

Operational playbook: common incidents
- Incident: obs-ingester sustained 503s -> escalation
  1) Pager triggers for ingest_lag_p95 > 2m OR escrow_fill > 70% for 5m.
  2) Triage: SRE on-call checks obs-ingester cluster health (kubectl/pgrep), resource saturation (GPU/CPU/memory), and ingress QPS.
  3) Short-term mitigations: enable shedding policy for noise traffic, increase ingestion capacity (scale replicas), or route non-critical tenants to deferred-mode (best-effort ingestion, immediate escrow).
  4) Post-incident: run the Escrow Reconciliation Procedure (see below) and create an incident RCA with telemetry-linked fingerprints.

Escrow Reconciliation Procedure (numbered)
1) Lock: mark escrow-service in read-only replay mode to prevent concurrent writes.
2) Audit: generate a reconciliation report listing escrowed fingerprints grouped by tenant and ingest-target.
3) Replay in controlled batches: 5000 records / minute per tenant, verify forward success via fingerprint ACKs.
4) Verify: cross-check forward ACKs against slo-eval and billing ledger for attribution.
5) Purge: after verification window, purge successfully forwarded records.
6) Report: publish reconciliation report to the incident ticket and add related fingerprints to the service RCA.

Safety and privacy controls
- PII redaction checklist: prompt content must be hashed or redacted before leaving the service boundary unless explicit debug mode is enabled for a short window and approved by security.
- Tenant encryption: for tenants who require private key isolation, escrow stores payloads encrypted with tenant-KMS keys and logs key usage events.
- Audit trail: every escrow write/replay/purge action must be appended to an append-only audit log (immutable S3 + signed manifest).

Developer guidance for service authors
- Use the telemetry client library (telemetry-client v2) and call emit_anchored(metric, envelope) at the earliest possible point in request handling.
- Avoid constructing envelopes client-side without calling library helper — the helper ensures HMAC and redaction.
- If your service processes high-volume short-lived requests (QPS > 1k per replica) enable prefix sampling hints to reduce payload sizes.

Telemetry client example (Python)
```python
from telemetry_client import TelemetryClient
client = TelemetryClient()
envelope = client.new_envelope(request_id=request_id, tenant_id=tenant)
client.emit_anchored("token_latency_ms", value=42, envelope=envelope)
```

Monitoring and dashboards (minimum set)
- Escrow: escrow_fill_pct (by tenant), escrow_forward_rate, escrow_replay_failures, escrow_purge_count.
- Pipeline: obs_ingest_lag_p50/p95, ingest_success_rate, forward_error_rate_by_code.
- Quality: anchored_telemetry_completeness (percentage of critical flows with envelope), envelope_integrity_failure_rate.

Rollout and migration plan (for services without anchoring)
1) Phase 0 — inventory (2 weeks): run the Anchoring Coverage Scanner to detect services that emit telemetry without envelopes.
2) Phase 1 — library adoption (4 weeks): add telemetry-client v2 to services and enable default envelope creation in dev environment.
3) Phase 2 — canary (2 weeks): enable anchoring for 5% of traffic for a small set of tenants; validate fingerprint pass-through and no regressions to ingestion.
4) Phase 3 — ramp (4 weeks): increase to 50% then 100% with SRE monitoring and a rollback flag.
5) Phase 4 — enforcement (ongoing): make anchored telemetry the baseline; services emitting unanchored telemetry will be rate-limited by the gateway.
